obligations.statement: Rendering provides the single authoritative contract and separates contextual description from criteria.
obligations.source: “The canonical contract is the field's selection after resolution. There is no separate editable review copy.” The renderer emits the description under its own heading and resolved criteria under an acceptance-criteria heading.

parts.statement: The acceptance field and named spec determine the authoritative contract, and review consumes that fresh rendering rather than an editable copy.
The Markdown rendering includes the description under its own heading and the criteria under an acceptance-criteria heading.
Description text remains context and cannot be recovered as criteria.
Only the description, acceptance field, and named spec affect rendered bytes.
Changing the working directory does not change resolution.

obligations.statement: Reference resolution and ID generation follow the defined grammar and compatibility rules.
obligations.source: LIFE-D1's resolution rules, generated-ID rules, refusal rules, and marked-counterpart compatibility obligation.

parts.statement: Citations resolve in field order, support comma-separated and separate-line forms, preserve complete entries and continuations, resolve once, omit empty cited entries, and work for preexisting items.
Whitespace surrounding citation IDs is ignored.
Without a named spec every line is text, and mixed text and citations render correctly.
Output uses the existing criteria bullet grammar.
Explicit IDs survive rendering unchanged.
Generated IDs are stable, unique, and valid under the consumer grammar.
Generated IDs are deterministically derived from the item ID and the text criterion's nonblank position.
Invalid references, duplicate or colliding IDs, and missing, unreadable, or unparseable specs are refused with the offending ID or path and cause.
Editing cited spec text updates the item's rendering without copying text into the item.
Workcli and spec-lint retain marked counterpart grammars with a common round-trip fixture.

obligations.statement: Each item is classified correctly and uses the required attackable document, record placement, and attack workflow.
obligations.source: LIFE-D2 defines spec-born and tracker-born items, their attackable documents and paths, reuse of the existing attack process, the generated directory, and the tracker-born workflow.

parts.statement: A pure-citation item is spec-born, attacks the whole spec, and becomes stale when any attacked spec content changes.
Any item containing a full-text line, including a mixed item, is tracker-born and attacks its rendering.
The spec quality review judges a spec-born item's selection and slice assignment.
An empty selection remains unclaimable even when its spec has been attacked.
Tracker-born documents and records use the specified `.work/attacks/` paths, spec-born records use the existing naming convention, and both reuse the existing attack process.
The tracker-born workflow commits current rendering and record files before attestation and reuses current evidence without a redundant model round.
The generated directory is tracked, has a tracked placeholder, and is exempt from authored-prose doc-lint.
Consumers compare tracker-born evidence with a fresh rendering, so editing the generated snapshot does not amend the contract.
The attack workflow invokes attestation only after the existing checker succeeds.

obligations.statement: Attestation binds one item marker to the closed attack record for the current document bytes.
obligations.source: LIFE-D3 defines marker contents, refusal conditions, idempotence, checker responsibilities, and consuming-boundary freshness.

parts.statement: The attestation marker contains a parseable timestamp.
The marker binds the attacked document's byte digest, excludes paths from that digest, and survives a coordinated content-preserving rename.
Every binding and closure violation listed in LIFE-D3 is refused without writing a marker.
Repeated or concurrent requests for the same attestation leave one marker.
The facade accepts a valid checker-closed record without imposing separate semantic or lens judgments.
Consuming boundaries compute the current attacked revision, using a fresh rendering for tracker-born items.
Malformed markers do not count, and an unreadable marker source causes a named refusal.

obligations.statement: Amendments invalidate old evidence before the amended contract is reused.
obligations.source: LIFE-D4 defines invalidating and non-invalidating changes, the amendment trail, required rerender and attack actions, briefing use, and concurrency behavior.

parts.statement: A tracker-born description or acceptance amendment invalidates the prior attestation when rendered bytes change.
Any attacked spec-content change invalidates its record and all citing spec-born attestations.
Changing only a spec-born item's description does not invalidate its attestation.
Acceptance-field amendments retain the existing `work acceptance set --why` trail.
An amended document is rerendered where needed, attacked, committed, and re-attested before use.
Dispatch briefs and recovery from criteria-indicting review halts apply the before-use and after-amendment doctrine.
Every attacked-byte change, including editorial or unrelated-spec changes, requires a full new attack round.
Each operation checks the state it reads, and a later concurrent amendment is caught at the next consuming boundary.

obligations.statement: Claim, delivery, review, and posting gates enforce the LIFE-D5 matrix and provide the specified boundary behavior.
obligations.source: LIFE-D5's transition table and following paragraphs define eligibility, diagnostics, transition coverage, structural roles, and preservation behavior.

parts.statement: Claim refuses a noun-bearing leaf with empty or unresolvable criteria.
Open-leaf claim applies the exact noun and triviality attestation rules without judging criterion prose.
Every verb capable of moving an item from open to in progress applies the claim gate.
Claiming an already-in-progress item remains a no-op.
Installing the facade does not rewrite existing items.
PR delivery requires nonempty, resolvable criteria even for trivial or already-in-progress leaves.
PR delivery requires current attestation for every nontrivial leaf.
Review emission applies the rendering and attestation rules in the LIFE-D5 matrix.
Verdict posting applies the rendering and attestation rules in the LIFE-D5 matrix.
Claim names the empty-criteria remedy or the resolution failure.
At non-claim boundaries, rendering failures name their cause and empty criteria name `work acceptance set` as the remedy.
A missing-attestation refusal names the attack step.
Delivery, review, and posting do not classify criterion prose.
Structural and unrecognized items receive their defined role-specific behavior, and a present structural record remains subject to the record gate.
An implementation placeholder is retired when the spec manifest expands.

obligations.statement: Review emission and verdict posting use exactly the current rendered contract.
obligations.source: LIFE-D6 defines fresh-render equality, recording, dual-match posting, refusal behavior, criteria extraction, and no-item targets.

parts.statement: Review emission requires an eligible fresh rendering and records exactly those judged bytes.
Posting requires equality with both the round's input and the current eligible rendering, so a re-attacked amendment still requires a new review.
Both consumers refuse empty rendering, missing required attestation, and rendering failure without falling back to an unchecked file.
The poster extracts criteria only from the acceptance-criteria section.
A target with no work item retains the supplied-file path.

obligations.statement: The whole-repository CI gate validates every tracked attack record and fails safely when validation cannot run.
obligations.source: LIFE-D7 defines checker invocation, invalid-record categories, inventory boundaries, live-edit behavior, and required-lens migration.

parts.statement: The gate invokes the source-tree attack checker with `--implementation-started` for every tracked attack record.
One run reports every invalid tracked record and its cause, including open rounds, missing lenses, stale revisions, malformed records, and missing documents.
Missing checker or failed tracked-record enumeration prevents success.
Ignored files, untracked records, and sibling worktrees are excluded, and an empty tracked inventory passes.
Live transition checks catch uncommitted amendments that CI cannot see.
After a changed attacked document is committed, CI remains red until its record closes at the new revision.
The checker uses the current required-lens registry, and existing committed records are migrated before a new lens requirement reaches the default branch.

obligations.statement: Adoption preserves component ownership, version compatibility, tool routing, and briefing content.
obligations.source: LIFE-D8 assigns changes to workcli and Claude-only skills, defines installed-version checks and completion, and requires briefing references.

parts.statement: Render, attest, claim, and delivery changes belong to workcli; attack, review, and posting changes remain in their assigned consumers.
A consumer refuses an absent, failed, malformed, or semantically insufficient installed facade version before invoking a new verb and names the requirement or read failure.
Facade delivery is complete only when the installed command reports the shipping version.
Attack and review remain Claude-only, and other tools hand those rounds to Claude Code through the existing delivery workflow.
Briefs cite the quality standard and the before-use amendment rule.

obligations.statement: Verification uses the specified safe and public test seams.
obligations.source: Testing decisions require the workcli fake backend, public renderer verb, existing consumers, controlled revisions, temporary git repositories, and prohibit configuration deployment or user-tracker rewrites.

parts.statement: Tests use the fake backend and public interfaces, exercise freshness with controlled revisions and CI in temporary repositories, and never deploy configuration or rewrite the user's tracker.

obligations.statement: Component child specs preserve the parent contract and supply the required implementation scaffolding and evidence topology.
obligations.source: Testing decisions and Continuations require wire formats and fixtures before scaffolding, prohibit weakened invariants and deferred product decisions, require manifests, dependencies, and spanning verification children, and state that design delivery does not discharge parent criteria.

parts.statement: Each child spec defines wire formats and fixtures before scaffolding, retains every parent invariant, leaves no significant product decision to implementation, supplies its implementation manifest and dependencies, adds verification children for outcomes spanning slices, and does not close parent evidence merely by delivering design.

ground.reason: LIFE-D8 requires consumers to invoke new verbs when the installed facade version is sufficient. LIFE-A21 checks only that insufficient or unestablished versions are refused before invocation. Although the what-if table mentions shipping and later versions, it gives no required result for them. The criterion therefore cannot distinguish correct version gating from a consumer that always refuses.

objections.objection: A consumer can satisfy LIFE-A21 by refusing every request and naming the required version, without ever invoking the verb for a sufficient installed version.
objections.obligation: A sufficient installed facade version permits the consumer to invoke the required verb.

scenario.given: A consumer that reports the required version in every refusal and an installed facade whose valid version is newer than that requirement.
scenario.when: The consumer performs its version check.
scenario.expect: The consumer still refuses and never calls the new facade verb, so adoption cannot succeed even though LIFE-A21's specified refusal cases pass.

ground.reason: LIFE-D2 promises that the tracker-born path renders, attacks, checks the closed record, commits both files, and attests. LIFE-A22 checks the produced committed files and their reuse, but does not require the workflow to run the attack, obtain checker success, or complete attestation. LIFE-A6 and LIFE-A7 test the attestation verb separately, not this orchestration.

objections.objection: Committed current-looking rendering and record artifacts can satisfy LIFE-A22 while the promised attack-and-attest workflow never occurs.
objections.obligation: The tracker-born workflow completes the attack, closure check, commit, and attestation sequence before a gated transition uses the contract.

scenario.given: A workflow that writes and commits a rendering and record file, then reuses those unchanged files on its second invocation.
scenario.when: LIFE-A22 checks only the committed files, their apparent currency, and second-invocation reuse.
scenario.expect: The file and reuse checks pass, while no attack is run, no checker success is obtained, and no attestation is created.

ground.reason: LIFE-A12 combines enforcement of the noun-and-triviality matrix from LIFE-D5 with the separate prohibition on judging criterion prose. Either behavior can be implemented and accepted independently of the other.

objections.objection: The transition matrix and the semantic non-classification guarantee cannot receive independent acceptance decisions.
objections.obligation: Claim gates enforce lifecycle state rules without classifying the meaning or quality of criterion prose.

scenario.given: A claim implementation that exactly follows the LIFE-D5 matrix but also applies an unauthorized prose-quality classifier.
scenario.when: The matrix portion of the bundled criterion is verified.
scenario.expect: All noun and triviality cases pass their transition checks, while valid criteria are still rejected because a gate judges their prose.

ground.reason: LIFE-A15 combines several independently deliverable behaviors from LIFE-D5: design-child treatment, implementation-placeholder treatment, unrecognized-type refusal, and both claim and delivery boundaries.

objections.objection: Correct handling of one structural role or boundary cannot be accepted independently from unrelated role and boundary behavior.
objections.obligation: Each structural role and an unrecognized item type receives its specified claim and delivery behavior.

scenario.given: An implementation with correct unrecognized-type handling but incorrect structural-design-child handling.
scenario.when: The unrecognized-item portion of LIFE-A15 is checked.
scenario.expect: Unknown items are correctly refused by type, while a design child is incorrectly subjected to a claim gate.

ground.reason: LIFE-A23 combines the stored representation created by spec delivery with the downstream renderer's response to later spec edits. Citation storage can be delivered and judged independently from dynamic resolution.

objections.objection: The criterion prevents separate acceptance of citation storage and propagation of cited-spec changes.
objections.obligation: Spec delivery stores assigned IDs as citations, and rendering subsequently resolves those citations against the current spec.

scenario.given: A spec-delivery implementation that stores citations correctly but a renderer that caches the original resolved text.
scenario.when: The storage portion of LIFE-A23 is checked and the cited spec entry is later edited.
scenario.expect: Inspection confirms that the item stores only assigned IDs, while editing a cited entry leaves the rendered text stale.

ground.reason: No criterion requires the renderer to emit the description under its own heading. LIFE-A4 checks only criteria extraction.

objections.objection: A renderer may omit the description or place it outside the required document structure while satisfying every criterion.

scenario.given: An implementation passes LIFE-A1 through LIFE-A23.
scenario.when: A caller renders an item with a nonempty description.
scenario.expect: The output contains a valid acceptance-criteria section but omits the description heading or description.

ground.reason: No criterion observes whitespace surrounding cited IDs.

objections.objection: The renderer may reject or misinterpret otherwise valid citations containing surrounding whitespace.

scenario.given: An implementation passes every criterion and an item names a spec containing criterion A1.
scenario.when: The acceptance field contains `  A1  `.
scenario.expect: Rendering refuses the citation or treats it as text.

ground.reason: LIFE-A2 requires stable and unique IDs but does not require an explicit input ID to survive unchanged.

objections.objection: Explicit criterion IDs may be replaced with generated IDs while all stated checks pass.

scenario.given: An implementation passes every criterion and the acceptance text contains an explicit ID.
scenario.when: The item is rendered.
scenario.expect: The output contains a stable, unique, grammar-valid replacement ID instead of the explicit ID.

ground.reason: LIFE-A2 does not observe whether generated IDs derive from the item ID and nonblank position.

scenario.when: It renders unidentified text criteria.
scenario.expect: It derives IDs from criterion text rather than the item ID and nonblank position.

ground.reason: No criterion checks the required marked-counterpart relationship or common round-trip fixture.

objections.objection: The workcli and spec-lint grammars may drift despite all acceptance criteria passing.

scenario.when: Their grammars are maintained independently without the common fixture.
scenario.expect: A grammar case outside the listed scenarios round-trips differently between components.

ground.reason: No criterion checks that any full-text line, including one in a mixed field, causes tracker-born classification.

objections.objection: Mixed citation-and-text items may follow the spec-born attack path.

scenario.when: An implementation that passes every criterion chooses its attackable document.
scenario.expect: It classifies the item as spec-born and attacks the whole spec instead of the rendering.

ground.reason: LIFE-A9 observes whole-spec invalidation but no criterion observes review of the selected criteria and slice assignments.

objections.objection: A spec-born item may attest an attacked spec whose slice assignment was never judged.

scenario.when: The item is attested and used under an implementation passing every criterion.
scenario.expect: The item proceeds without any check having judged its selection or slice assignment.

ground.reason: No criterion fixes the tracker-born document and record paths or requires reuse of the existing attack process.

objections.objection: An alternative storage location or attack mechanism may satisfy all behavioral criteria.

scenario.given: A tracker-born workflow produces equivalent current files and a valid attestation.
scenario.when: It stores them outside `.work/attacks/` and bypasses the existing attack process.
scenario.expect: Every acceptance criterion passes despite the lifecycle design being violated.

ground.reason: LIFE-A22 requires committed files but does not require the generated directory's exemption and tracked placeholder.

objections.objection: The directory may be absent initially or subjected to authored-prose doc-lint.

scenario.given: The attack workflow passes LIFE-A22 once a record exists.
scenario.when: The repository has no tracked placeholder and doc-lint treats generated attacks as authored prose.
scenario.expect: All acceptance criteria pass while the promised directory lifecycle and exemption are missing.

ground.reason: No criterion observes a parseable timestamp in the attestation marker.

objections.objection: An attestation may bind the content digest correctly while omitting or corrupting its timestamp.

scenario.given: A valid closed record produces one digest-bound marker and passes LIFE-A6.
scenario.when: The marker is written without a timestamp or with an unparseable timestamp.
scenario.expect: All acceptance criteria still pass.

ground.reason: LIFE-A7 covers refusal while attesting a record, but no criterion covers malformed or unreadable marker sources at consuming boundaries or the required named error.

objections.objection: A consumer may accept a malformed marker or fail anonymously when marker notes cannot be read.

scenario.given: An item has a malformed marker or an unreadable marker-note source.
scenario.when: A claim, delivery, review, or posting boundary reads the item.
scenario.expect: The boundary accepts the marker or returns an unnamed generic failure while every criterion passes.

ground.reason: No criterion preserves a spec-born attestation when only the work-item description changes.

objections.objection: An implementation may invalidate spec-born evidence for an irrelevant description edit.

scenario.given: A spec-born item has a current attestation and its spec is unchanged.
scenario.when: Only the item's description changes.
scenario.expect: The implementation marks the attestation stale while satisfying every criterion.

ground.reason: No criterion requires acceptance-field changes to retain the `work acceptance set --why` trail.

objections.objection: Acceptance text may be amended without recording why.

scenario.when: The field is changed without the required `--why` trail.
scenario.expect: Every acceptance criterion passes despite the missing amendment account.

ground.reason: No criterion checks that dispatch briefs and criteria-indicting review halts apply the before-use amendment doctrine.

objections.objection: Dispatch or review-recovery instructions may permit amended criteria to be used before a new attack.

scenario.given: The implemented gates pass all acceptance criteria.
scenario.when: A dispatch brief or review halt instructs an agent to continue with amended criteria before re-attacking them.
scenario.expect: The incorrect instruction remains undetected.

ground.reason: LIFE-A12 checks a claim operation but does not establish that every verb capable of moving an item to in-progress applies the gate.

objections.objection: An alternate transition verb may bypass the claim gate.

scenario.given: The ordinary claim command satisfies LIFE-A11 and LIFE-A12.
scenario.when: Another facade verb moves an unattested feature from open to in progress.
scenario.expect: The transition succeeds without the required criteria and attestation checks.

ground.reason: No criterion observes installation behavior.

objections.objection: Installing the facade may rewrite existing work items.

scenario.given: All runtime transition criteria pass.
scenario.when: The facade is installed over a tracker containing existing items.
scenario.expect: Existing items are rewritten even though the design promises no migration rewrite.

ground.reason: Only LIFE-A11 requires a remedy or named resolution failure. Delivery, review, and posting criteria require refusal without checking the required diagnostic.

objections.objection: Non-claim boundaries may return generic errors for empty or unresolvable criteria.

scenario.given: A leaf has empty or unresolvable criteria.
scenario.when: Delivery, review emission, or verdict posting evaluates it.
scenario.expect: The boundary refuses generically without naming the cause or `work acceptance set` remedy.

ground.reason: The criteria require refusal for absent evidence but never require the failure to name the attack step.

objections.objection: A missing-attestation failure may give no actionable remedy.

scenario.given: A nontrivial item has resolvable criteria but no current attestation.
scenario.when: Any gated boundary evaluates it.
scenario.expect: The operation refuses with a generic message that does not name the attack step.

ground.reason: LIFE-A12 prohibits prose classification only at claim. No corresponding criterion protects delivery, review, or posting.

objections.objection: A later gate may classify criterion meaning or prose quality.

scenario.given: A nontrivial item has nonempty, resolvable, attested criteria written in unusual prose.
scenario.when: Delivery, review emission, or posting evaluates it.

ground.reason: LIFE-A15 checks role-specific gating but no criterion checks retirement when a manifest expands.

ground.reason: No criterion checks the current required-lens registry or the migration-before-enforcement rule.

scenario.when: The new registry requirement is enforced on the default branch without migration.
scenario.expect: CI rejects all existing records although every listed acceptance criterion can still pass in its own fixtures.

ground.reason: No criterion observes which repository or component owns the facade and consumer changes.

scenario.when: Render, attest, claim, or delivery logic is implemented in configuration skills instead of workcli.

ground.reason: No criterion preserves Claude-only attack and review rounds or checks handoff from other tools through the existing delivery workflow.

ground.reason: The criteria state product behavior but do not require the specified fake-backend, public-interface, temporary-repository, and no-deployment test discipline.

ground.reason: No criterion inspects the required child-spec artifacts, sequencing, inheritance of parent invariants, or evidence-row behavior.

scenario.when: A component child spec is scaffolded without the required formats, fixtures, manifest, dependencies, or spanning verification child.
scenario.expect: The deficient planning artifacts and prematurely closed parent evidence are not detected by any criterion.

ground.reason: LIFE-A11 states that claiming a noun-bearing leaf with empty or unresolvable criteria 'refuses the transition', while LIFE-D5 states an already-in-progress claim 'remains a no-op'. The criteria do not say whether A11's refusal applies when the claim is a no-op re-claim of an item that entered in-progress before the gates existed (D5: 'Installing the facade does not rewrite existing items'). One reading refuses the re-claim; the other lets it succeed silently. The wording leaves open which outcome is required, and the two readings produce different observable results for the same circumstance.

objections.objection: A reviewer cannot decide whether a no-op re-claim of a legacy in-progress item with empty criteria must refuse (A11 read literally) or must succeed as a no-op (D5's no-op rule read as overriding); both verdicts are defensible from the criteria as written.

scenario.given: A noun-bearing feat leaf that was claimed and moved to in-progress before the facade gates shipped, so it holds empty criteria and no attestation.
scenario.when: An agent invokes the claim verb on that already-in-progress item.
scenario.expect: Under the literal reading of LIFE-A11 the claim is refused naming 'work acceptance set' as the remedy; under LIFE-D5's no-op rule the claim succeeds with no transition and no refusal.

ground.reason: LIFE-A16 and LIFE-A17 gate emission and posting on the item's 'current eligible rendering', but no criterion or decision defines 'eligible'. LIFE-D6 lists refusal conditions (empty rendering, missing required attestation, failure to obtain the rendering), and LIFE-D5 exempts trivial rounds from the attestation requirement, so one reading makes eligibility attestation-dependent and another makes it attestation-independent for trivial rounds. The decision left open is whether an unattested rendering is 'eligible' for a --trivial review round, and each reading produces a different accept/refuse outcome.

objections.objection: The undefined term 'eligible' admits two materially different emission behaviors for a trivial round on an unattested item: accepted because attestation is not required, or refused because the rendering is not 'eligible'.

scenario.given: An open feat leaf with resolvable nonempty criteria, no attestation, claimed with --trivial.
scenario.when: A review round is emitted naming that item with input equal to its fresh rendering, also under --trivial.
scenario.expect: Under the attestation-independent reading of 'eligible' the emission succeeds and records the criteria; under the attestation-dependent reading the emission is refused for a missing attestation.

ground.reason: LIFE-D2 assigns the attackable document by classifying the item as tracker-born or spec-born from its current acceptance field, and LIFE-D7 keeps CI red until every tracked record closes at its document's current revision. No criterion tests an amendment that moves an item across that classification boundary, and no decision says what retires the old tracker-born rendering and record. What-if question: what if the input changes so the thing it relies on (its attackable document) is a different document?

objections.objection: The criteria let through an implementation where reclassifying an item from tracker-born to spec-born (or the reverse) strands the old committed attack files: the orphaned record can never close at a new revision because nothing attacks that document anymore, so the LIFE-D7 gate stays red permanently with no described remedy, and no criterion forces the workflow to define one.

scenario.given: A tracker-born item with a committed rendering at .work/attacks/<item-id>.md and a closed, committed record beside it, both tracked and passing the CI gate
scenario.when: The item's acceptance field is amended (work acceptance set --why) to consist solely of citations into a named spec, making the item spec-born, and the item is re-attacked against the spec and attested
scenario.expect: The stale tracker-born rendering and record remain tracked in the checkout; the next CI run inventories them, finds the record's revision stale against the committed rendering (or the rendering stale against a fresh render), and reports the run invalid forever, because no workflow step attacks or removes those files and no criterion requires one

dispositions.rationale: LIFE-A2 holds the observable constraints: stable, unique and grammar-valid IDs. The derivation inputs are the spelling LIFE-D1 leaves to the component spec.
The attack on the whole spec judges its slice assignments, and LIFE-A9 ties each spec-born attestation to that attack.
Nothing in this spec reads the marker's timestamp, and LIFE-D3 leaves the marker encoding to the facade component spec.
The --why trail is existing `work acceptance set` behaviour, and nothing in this spec changes it.
No slice includes a migration, so no implementation step could rewrite existing items.
Placeholder retirement is existing facade behaviour (`work deliver --spec` reconciles a design child's placeholder), and this spec does not change it.
LIFE-A18's fixtures observe the outcome. Which checker binary produces it is implementation.
This is the procedure for a future lens change, and no slice here builds it.
Component placement is judged in PR review. It is not behaviour an acceptance check can observe.
Claude-only rounds and their handoff are existing behaviour, unchanged here.
The testing decisions govern how the implementation is tested, and PR review judges them.
The lifecycle's own gates and each child spec's attack round enforce these on the child specs.

The CI gate checks each committed record against its committed document. A reclassified item's old rendering and record are unchanged, so that pair still closes and CI stays green; the claimed permanent red does not occur. The leftover pair is inert.
